hero.subtitle: When you run out of words, we give them to you.
hero.text_1: This is not an 'HR guide'. This is a survival tool for you who have been subjected to workplace bullying, ostracism, or inappropriate treatment.
hero.text_2: We offer words for difficult situations, tools for documentation, and understanding of what is happening to you. You are not crazy, and you are not alone.

dialog.title: How does Safe Wing work?
dialog.desc: Safe Wing is designed to restore your agency in a situation where it has been taken away.
dialog.step1_text: The first step is to understand what is happening. Is it bullying? Or bad management? Naming reduces chaos.
dialog.step2_text: Memory is unreliable under stress. Record events immediately, but safely. Facts are your best protection.
dialog.step3_text: Bullying is not your fault. Learn to recognize tactics like gaslighting or ostracism so you can protect yourself.
dialog.step4_text: When you are ready, you get concrete action steps. How to bring it up? How to file a report? How to survive?

why.title: Why does this exist?
why.p1: Workplace bullying is violence that hides behind 'interaction problems' and 'humor'. It destroys self-esteem, health, and careers.
why.list_1: It is often impossible for the victim to defend themselves alone.
why.list_2: Organizations often protect themselves, not the victim.
why.list_3: The burden of proof falls on the exhausted victim.
why.list_4: We want to change the power dynamics.
why.conclusion_2: Your reaction is a normal reaction to an abnormal situation.

comparison.title: Is this bullying?
comparison.p1: Bullying is not always shouting. It is often silent: avoiding eye contact, withholding information, forgetting from meetings.
comparison.p2: It is when you feel in your stomach that something is wrong, but you are told that 'you are just imagining it'.
comparison.p4: Occasional rudeness is not bullying. Bullying is repeated and continuous.
comparison.p5: If you are constantly on guard when going to work, it is no longer just about 'chemistry'.
comparison.p6: Explore different forms of bullying and learn to recognize what is happening to you.
comparison.quote: "It's not a conflict if only one person is being hit."

log.title: Private Log
log.subtitle: Write it down. Do it now.
log.text: When you are stressed, your memory fails. The bully relies on that. Don't give them that advantage.
log.label: PRIVATE & ENCRYPTED
log.footer_1: We do not store your data in the cloud.
log.footer_3: You can download a PDF report anytime.

early.title: Why is documentation important?
early.p1: Occupational safety, doctors, and unions ask first: 'Do you have examples written down?'
early.p2: When you have black on white, the conversation changes from 'he said she said' to fact-based.
early.research_1: Documentation restores a sense of control.
early.research_2: Keeping a diary reduces stress symptoms.

freedom.title: You have the power
freedom.p1: We do not decide for you. We do not tell you to resign, nor do we force you to fight.
freedom.quote: "Courage is not the absence of fear. Courage is acting despite fear."
freedom.p2: We give you a map and a compass. You choose the route.

final.title: Are you ready?
final.subtitle: The first step is the hardest. Take it now.
final.disclaimer_1: THIS SERVICE DOES NOT REPLACE A DOCTOR OR POLICE.
final.disclaimer_2: IF YOU ARE IN IMMEDIATE DANGER, CALL EMERGENCY NUMBER 112.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: You are not alone with these questions.
faq.q1: How do I know if it is bullying or just 'bad chemistry'?
faq.a1: Chemistry is mutual. Bullying is one-sided and repeated. If you feel constant anxiety, are on guard, or systematically invalidated, it is likely bullying.
faq.q2: What if I am imagining everything?
faq.a2: Victims often question their experience ('am I just sensitive?'). This is a normal reaction to an abnormal situation. Your feelings are real.
faq.q3: Should I make an official report?
faq.a3: Sometimes. It depends on your organization's culture and your resources. We help you assess the risks and benefits before acting.
faq.a4: Yes, but it often requires outside intervention or a change in dynamics. It is difficult to change the situation alone.
faq.a5: Write down: What happened, who was present, date and time. Keep emails. Do not record secretly, it may be illegal.
faq.a6: Your health is paramount. Sometimes leaving is the bravest act. Check waiting periods and financial security before deciding.
faq.a7: Occupational health, shop steward, occupational safety representative, and union are primary parties. Mieli Ry also offers conversation help.
faq.q9: How to act in an acute crisis?
faq.a9_text: Breathe. Leave the situation if possible.
faq.a9_list_1: **Call** a trusted friend or crisis helpline.
faq.a9_list_2: **Seek** a doctor if you are exhausted.
faq.a9_list_3: **Do not be alone** with your feelings.

hero.title: How do you experience the world?
hero.description_1: Empathy is not one thing. It is a complex puzzle of cognition, emotions, and morality.
hero.description_2: This test does not judge you. It helps you understand your strengths and blind spots in a changing world.

cognitive.title: Cognitive
cognitive.desc: Ability to logically take another's perspective.

affective.title: Affective
affective.desc: Ability to feel another's emotions in the body.

moral.title: Moral

questions.1: I usually understand easily why someone is upset about something.
questions.2: I can often predict how my colleague will react to my suggestion.
questions.3: It is easy for me to put myself in another's shoes, even if I disagree.
questions.4: I quickly notice if someone is pretending to be happy when they are not.
questions.5: When I see someone suffering, I feel bad myself.
questions.6: Others' enthusiasm spreads to me easily.
questions.7: I empathize strongly with the fates of characters in movies and books.
questions.8: It is hard for me to stay calm if a loved one is having a hard time.
questions.9: I feel a duty to intervene if I see someone being treated unfairly.
questions.10: I am ready to put my own tasks aside to help a colleague in distress.
questions.11: Justice is a more important value to me than sticking to rules.
questions.12: I cannot watch from the sidelines if a weaker person is discriminated against.

results.cognitive_desc: You understand people on a thought level.

context_factors.trauma: Trauma can shut down emotional connection.
context_factors.neurodiversity: Neurodiversity changes the way empathy is experienced.

results.disclaimer: This is an indicative test, not a diagnosis.

helper.title: The Helper
helper.description: You want to save everyone, sometimes at the expense of your own coping. Remember to put the oxygen mask on yourself first.

outsider.title: The Outsider
outsider.description: You may have withdrawn to protect yourself. It is an understandable reaction, but connection to others is important for recovery.

defender.title: The Defender
defender.description: Justice is everything to you. You are the one who dares to speak up when others are silent.

observer.title: The Observer
observer.description: You understand situations accurately, but do not always dare to intervene. Your analytical nature is a strength, as long as it doesn't lead to passivity.

sensor.title: The Sensor
sensor.description: You feel changes in the atmosphere in your body quickly. This sensitivity is a gift, but requires strong boundaries.

growing.title: The Grower
growing.description: You are learning new ways to connect. Every step towards understanding is a victory.

analysis_steps.title: Act
analysis_steps.desc: Choose a safe way to intervene.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: You see your colleague Marja being criticized baselessly and sarcastically in a team meeting. Marja looks paralyzed and stares at the table.

choices.text: Move to sit next to Marja and ask quietly: 'Are you okay?'
choices.feedback: Research: Mere physical presence and asking 'Are you okay?' reduces the victim's anxiety by up to 40%.

choices.text: Challenge the bully directly in the meeting: 'Stop that immediately!'
choices.feedback: Direct confrontation can escalate and increase your own risk, although it is brave.

steps.speaker: Marja
steps.text: Marja glances at you gratefully and takes a deep breath. The bully slows down their speech noticing that Marja is no longer alone.

choices.text: Name the situation factually: 'Shall we continue with the agenda? Marja's input was important here.'
choices.feedback: Showing solidarity publicly stabilizes the situation without a fight.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The bully turns to you: 'Well look, someone's being sensitive today! Do you have a club going on?' The atmosphere tightens.

choices.text: Stay calm: 'It's about workplace rules, not sensitivity.'
choices.feedback: Calmness is the best weapon when the other party tries to personalize the conflict.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: The meeting ends. Marja comes to thank you later. She says that without your support she might have burst into tears or left the room.

choices.feedback: Great! You are an active witness breaking the cycle of isolation.

steps.speaker: WhatsApp Group
steps.text: Mocking memes about the newest hobbyist start spreading in the group. No one comments anything, although 20 people have seen the messages.

choices.text: Write in the group: 'This doesn't belong here, do others agree?'
choices.feedback: By asking for others' opinion, you break 'pluralistic ignorance' and share responsibility.
Leaving is a sign, but it leaves the victim alone. Try intervening in the group.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: It's quiet for a moment, but then two other members thumbs-up your message and write: 'True, let's stick to the topic.' The Bystander Effect breaks.

choices.text: Suggest reviewing the rules to the admin

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: You are out of the group, but you know the mocking continues. You feel guilty and detached from the community.

choices.text: Send private message to victim: 'I saw the messages, they are not ok.'
choices.feedback: Even if you didn't intervene publicly, private support is vital for the victim.

steps.speaker: Narrator
steps.text: Your action encouraged others to intervene too. The group culture is now clearer and safer for everyone. You have broken pluralistic ignorance.

choices.feedback: An active bystander is the backbone of a healthy community. When one speaks, 'silent disapproval' turns into collective action.

difficult_conversations.title: Choose Your Opponent
difficult_conversations.subtitle: Who will you face today? Practice against different personalities.

ui.won_desc: You maintained your composure and authority beautifully.
ui.lost_desc: You lost either your composure or authority. Try again.

aggro.title: Steamroller
aggro.intro: Steamroller enters the room slamming doors.

dialogs.opponent: WHAT NOW?! I have real work to do, and no time to listen to your whining!

options.text: Don't yell at me! I won't listen to that!
options.reply: DON'T YOU ORDER ME AROUND!!

options.text: I notice you are agitated. I'll wait a moment.
options.reply: ... (Sighs heavily) Well?! Say your piece quickly.

options.text: (Silence) ...
options.reply: Do you have anything to say or can I leave?

dialogs.opponent: This project is late because of YOU! Don't try to shift the blame on me!

options.text: I'm not shifting blame, I'm trying to solve the problem. Let's talk facts.
options.reply: Facts?! Hah! Let's see your 'facts'.

options.text: It's not my fault!! You didn't deliver those numbers!
options.reply: That's enough! I won't listen to those lies!

options.text: Sorry, I'm trying my best...
options.reply: Your best is clearly not enough!

dialogs.opponent: I've been doing this job for 20 years! Don't come advising me!

options.text: I appreciate your experience. That's why I want cooperation to work.
options.reply: Hmmph. Well... experience is an asset.

options.text: The world changes, gramps.
options.reply: GET OUT OF MY OFFICE!

options.text: I'm not advising, just stating the rules.
options.reply: Rules... you and your rules.

victim.title: The Victim
victim.intro: The Victim sits down with a tissue in hand, tears in eyes.

dialogs.opponent: Why did you call me here? (Sniff) Have I done something wrong? I always do my best...

options.text: No worries, take a tissue. This isn't serious.
options.reply: I'm so afraid I'll get fired! (Crying intensifies)

options.text: I'd like to discuss the team atmosphere and your role in it.
options.reply: My role? So I'm guilty? Everyone hates me...

options.text: Stop that whining.
options.reply: You are cruel! A monster!

dialogs.opponent: I just can't take it anymore... no one understands me. You are always against me too.

options.text: I'm not against you. I want to support you, but we need to change how we communicate.
options.reply: Support? Do you really mean that?

options.text: Oh poor thing. Maybe you should rest.
options.reply: Yes I should... I'm going home. (Leaves abruptly)

options.text: That playing victim doesn't work on me.
options.reply: Playing victim?! I AM the victim here!

dialogs.opponent: If you write a note about this, my life is ruined! How can you do this to me?

options.text: This is a normal development discussion. I will record what was agreed.
options.reply: ...okay. If you promise to record honestly.

options.text: I won't record if you promise to improve.
options.reply: I promise! I promise anything! (Does not change behavior)

options.text: It is a consequence of your choices.
options.reply: (Stares silently, but stops crying)

gaslight.title: Gaslighter
gaslight.intro: Gaslighter looks at you smiling, completely calm.

dialogs.opponent: Hi. What's wrong? You look stressed. Is everything okay at home?

options.text: Don't change the subject. Let's talk about yesterday's meeting.
options.reply: Yesterday? Oh, where you raised your voice?

options.text: Just fine... just a bit tired.
options.reply: That's what I thought. You are overworked, imagining things.

options.text: That's not relevant.
options.reply: Of course it is. We are humans. I'm worried about you.

dialogs.opponent: I never said that. You misunderstood. Again.

options.text: I have the email here that says exactly that.
options.reply: Email? Show me. ... Hah, you are interpreting that completely wrong.

options.text: Maybe I remember wrong then...?
options.reply: Yes you do. You've been very forgetful lately.

options.text: I heard it with my own ears, and Peter heard it too.
options.reply: Peter? Peter says whatever to please you.

dialogs.opponent: Are you sure you are suitable for this role? You seem... unstable.

options.text: My competence is not the topic. The topic is your behavior.
options.reply: ... (Smile fades). Fine. Let's talk then.

options.text: What?! I am completely stable!
options.reply: Well that reaction doesn't seem very stable. Calm down now.

header.title: Neurodiversity is a Superpower
header.quote: ADHD, autism, and high sensitivity are not bugs. They are different operating systems.
header.intro: When we stop trying to force square pegs into round holes, we discover that different minds solve problems in unique and brilliant ways.

what.title: What is it?
what.subtitle: Common forms of neurodiversity
what.adhd: ADHD: A race car brain with bicycle brakes. Speed, creativity, but challenges in regulation.
what.autism: Autism: A specialist's mind. Deep focus, honesty, and systematic thinking.
what.dyslexia: Dyslexia: Visual thinking. Seeing the big picture instead of details.

superpowers.title: Superpowers
superpowers.subtitle: In the right environment
superpowers.productivity: Productivity: Capability for hyperfocus that surpasses neurotypicals.
superpowers.innovation: Innovation: Ability to think outside the box because you don't see the box.
superpowers.hyperfocus: Passion: Intense dedication to topics of interest.

spoon_theory.title: The Spoon Theory
spoon_theory.text: Imagine you have 12 spoons of energy for the day. A neurotypical uses 1 spoon to get ready for work. A neurodivergent might use 5 just to handle the sensory overload of the commute.

what.title: What is it?
what.text: A metaphor for limited energy resources.

save.title: Saves Spoons
save.text: Quiet, clear goals, autonomy, recovery time.

environment.title: Environment
environment.text: Open offices and constant notifications are kryptonite.

misunderstandings.title: Misunderstandings
misunderstandings.text: Direct communication is often interpreted as rudeness.

masking.title: Masking
masking.text: Masking: Hiding your true traits to fit in. It is exhausting and leads to burnout. "I'm fine" often means "I'm acting fine".

employee.title: For Employee
list: Know your manual: What do you need? Silence? Headphones?
Communicate needs: "I work best with written instructions."
Allow recovery: Respect your need for rest.

manager.title: For Manager
list: Stop assuming: lack of eye contact ≠ lack of listening.
Enable molding: Allow different ways of working.
Be direct: Say what you mean. Avoid hints.

decoder.title: Double Empathy Decoder
decoder.intro: Misunderstandings happen when two different operating systems interact.

items.nt: They are quiet. Are they poorly prepared?
items.nd: I am processing information. I need a moment to structure my answer precisely.
items.bridge: Give time to answer or an opportunity to answer in writing.

items.nt: They are antisocial and isolating from the team.
items.nd: I am protecting my senses to focus on work efficiently.
items.bridge: Respect the need for peace to work. Communicate via Slack.

items.nd: I am honest and efficient. Sticking to facts is a sign of respect.
items.bridge: Don't take criticism personally. Focus on the content.

hero.label: Youth at Work
hero.title: Work life is not a survival test.
hero.text: Is this your first job? Feel like you're being tested or asked the impossible? This is your guide to rights, boundaries, and how to identify exploitation.

intro.title: Why does this guide exist?
intro.text1: The position of youth in work life has changed. Recent studies show a worrying trend: young people experience more burnout and uncertainty than before.
intro.text2: The labor market situation in 2026 is challenging and fragmented. Especially worrying is the phenomenon where youth are used as "cheap and flexible labor", assuming they don't know their rights.

exploitation.title: Exploitation
exploitation.text: Unpaid "auditions", zero-hour contracts, and unpaid overtime in exchange for "being a good guy".

structural.title: Structural Bullying
structural.text: Youth don't know the collective agreement or fear for their fixed-term contracts. Bullying is withholding info or exclusion.

intro.quote: "The problem is not the youth's sensitivity – but the power dynamic."

career.title: Choose Your Path
career.subtitle: We analyze three common career paths from a well-being and risk perspective. Choose one to see expert analysis.

it_content.title: Analysis: Specialist Work
it_content.good: Autonomy protects from burnout. Job market often favors the employee.
it_content.expl: Unpaid overtime in the name of "process" or "proving yourself".
it_content.strat: Document all work in chat. Bound work time right at the start ("I'll do this tomorrow during work hours").

tech_content.title: Analysis: Craft and Tech
tech_content.good: Work result is visible. Clear hours: when the site melts, work ends. Strong unions.
tech_content.risk: Tough "macho culture" where hazing newcomes might be tradition.
tech_content.strat: Join a union immediately. Ask about safety out loud. ("I'll do this according to instructions.")

care_content.title: Analysis: Social & Education
care_content.good: Employment 100% certain. Work is extremely meaningful.
care_content.risk: Systemic burnout, resource shortage, and moral stress.
care_content.strat: Don't base identity on "calling". Keep breaks sacred. ("It's not safe to do this alone.")

interview.title: Identify a Toxic Workplace in the Interview
interview.q1: "How is onboarding organized and who is my mentor?"
interview.w1: ⚠️ If the answer is vague "it happens along the way", it's a warning sign.
interview.q2: "How is it handled here if a new employee makes a mistake?"
interview.w2_bad: ❌ Danger: "We expect things to be mastered quickly here."
interview.f1: "We are like one family here." (Code: no boundaries)
interview.f2: "Everyone started from zero sometime." (Code: justification for bad treatment)
interview.f3: "We don't watch the clock here." (Code: free overtime)

sim.title: First Summer Job?
sim.desc: Step into a realistic simulation where you learn to identify silent bullying and set professional boundaries.

recovery.title: When Scars Remain (Even After Work Ends)
recovery.desc: Workplace bullying doesn't stay at work – it stays in the body and mind. This is a normal reaction to an abnormal situation.
recovery.p1_text: Not because you are weak, but because you were judged by unfair rules. Your brain learns: "I am the problem."
recovery.p2_text: You constantly monitor others. You fear mistakes unreasonably. Body learns: "Work = Threat."
recovery.note: Do this for 3–5 situations. This exercise separates internalizing bullying.
recovery.final_quote: "You don't need 'courage'. You need safe repetitions."

generic.exhaustion_desc: You kept struggling without support. Your health failed before you could react. This is unfortunately a common story in healthcare.
generic.resignation_desc: You decided to protect yourself by leaving the situation. It is a brave act, but also a loss for the field.
generic.survival_desc: You used the Safe Wing. Documentation gave you factual data, and community support gave you strength. The fight is not over, but you are no longer alone.

manager.title: Simulation Ended
manager.desc: You have seen how "efficient" management can destroy a work community. Small, rationalized choices accumulated into a systemic failure.
manager.human_desc: Antti took 6 months of sick leave. Two other team members resigned due to the atmosphere of fear.
manager.reputation_desc: Insider information about poor management has spread. Recruitment has become difficult and brand image has collapsed.

neuro.burnout_desc: Finally the mask fell. Constant trying to adapt to a mold that doesn't yield took your strength. This is not a failure, but a sign that the environment must change.

youth.growth_desc: Congratulations. This was the hardest possible choice. You refused to take the blame for something that belonged to management responsibility. Although the situation was uncomfortable, you kept your self-respect. This skill will protect you throughout your career.
youth.burnout_desc: You waited for the situation to improve by itself. Unfortunately, in a toxic environment, silence is interpreted as permission to continue. Many young people burn out exactly like this. Remember: you have permission to leave.
youth.emotional_desc: You let emotions take over. It is human, but unfortunately in this environment it gave them a weapon against you. Next time: record facts, and talk about structures.
youth.key_learning_text: If a workplace requires you to endure bad treatment, the fault is not in you.
youth.protection_text: Always document lack of onboarding in email ("Just confirming that I understood correctly...").

fact_bank_page.description: Bullying is not just a feeling. It is a measurable, expensive, and destructive phenomenon. Here you can find the facts behind it.

page.intro: Emotions are messages. This mapping helps you articulate what might have been left behind by survival.

results.title: YOUR SITUATION
results.remember_text: This result is only a snapshot. It does not define you, but the situation you are in.

questions.validationText: Questioning one's memory is a typical consequence of manipulation.

questions.question: Do you feel invisible?

questions.validationText: Fear tells you that your boundaries have been violated.

questions.question: Do you not recognize yourself anymore?

header.title: Read Your Workplace
header.description: Learn to recognize if it's a normal conflict or a toxic atmosphere.

yellow.title: Yellow Sign
yellow.subtitle: Pay Attention
yellow.description: The first signs can be subtle.

quicktest.yes_desc: This meets the criteria for workplace bullying.
quicktest.no_desc: This is likely a normal conflict or inappropriate behavior, but not bullying.
quicktest.result_desc: This test helps distinguish between bullying and conflict. Keep practicing.

scenarios.text: The manager does not greet you in the mornings and avoids eye contact for weeks, even though they talk normally with others.
scenarios.explanation: This is ostracism, or social isolation. Repeated and systematic ignoring is psychological violence.

scenarios.text: A colleague disagrees with the project direction and you have a heated debate about arguments in a meeting.
scenarios.explanation: This is a normal work-related conflict. Disagreement on issues is not bullying provided it does not get personal.

scenarios.text: You are repeatedly not invited to team lunches and afterworks where everyone else participates.
scenarios.explanation: Exclusion from the group is one of the most common forms of indirect bullying.

scenarios.text: The manager gives you a warning for constant lateness.
scenarios.explanation: This is management authority. If the warning is based on facts and rules, it is not bullying.

header.label: SIMULATION
header.title: Practice difficult
header.p1: This is not a game. This is a tool to test your reactions and learn to identify bullying dynamics.

hero.subtitle: Documentation is your most important defense tool. Learn to do it so it stands up to scrutiny.

intro.title: Why is this important?
intro.text: Memory is unreliable, especially under stress. Written documentation is "hard data" that is difficult to dispute. It turns a vague experience into concrete evidence.
intro.memory_text: Logging immediately after an event is 10x more reliable than a week later.
intro.patterns_text: A single event can be explained as a misunderstanding. A series of 10 events is a pattern.

psych.title: Psychological Safety
psych.card1_text: When you write things down, you see black and white. It helps maintain your grip on reality when you are being gaslighted.
psych.card2_text: Writing is a way to move the event out of your head. It reduces rumination and helps you sleep.

formula.title: The 5-Point Formula
formula.subtitle: A good log always contains these five elements.

step1.title: Date & Time
step1.desc: When did it happen? Be precise.

step2.title: Location & Persons
step2.desc: Where were you? Who else was present (witnesses)?

step3.title: What happened?
step3.desc: Describe events objectively. Who said what? Who did what?

step4.title: Context
step4.desc: What happened right before? Was it a formal meeting or a hallway chat?

step5.title: Consequences
step5.desc: How did it end? How did you feel? Did it affect your work ability?

template.title: Copyable Template
template.content:
Date: DD.MM.YYYY at HH:MM
Location: [Location]
Attendees: [Names]

Description of Event:
[Person A] said/did [Action].
I responded [My Reaction].

Context:
The situation started when [Context].

Notes:
[Other observations, e.g., tone of voice, gestures]

followup.title: Follow-up
followup.text: If possible, send an email after the event confirming the content of the conversation. This creates a timestamp and a digital trail.
followup.example: "Thank you for the discussion. I want to confirm I understood correctly: you said that [X]. Did this also apply to situation [Y]?"

training.title: Training: Observation vs. Interpretation
training.subtitle: Learn to separate facts from emotions. Only facts have legal weight.

cards.bad: My boss was really mean to me again.
cards.good: My manager raised their voice and said my work laptop isn't mine.
cards.expl: "Mean" is an opinion. Raising a voice is an observable action.

cards.good: No one responded to my greeting in the coffee room at 9:00.
cards.expl: Describe the concrete situation, not the general vibe.

cards.bad: He tried to embarrass me on purpose.
cards.good: He laughed out loud when I made a mistake in the presentation.
cards.expl: You cannot know motives ("on purpose"), but you can log the laughter.

witness.title: Protecting Witnesses
witness.text: Remember that colleagues may be afraid to defend you. Log their presence, but don't force them to testify immediately.
list: Use names in your own notes.
If you share the document, consider changing names (Person A, Person B) in the first phase.

security.title: Data Security
security.dont_use_work: DO NOT USE WORK COMPUTER OR EMAIL FOR THESE NOTES.
list: Your employer may have the right to read your work email.
If you are fired, you lose access to tools immediately.
Use this app (data only on your device) or a personal notebook/laptop.

[Recipient: Manager/HR]

I am informing you that I have experienced inappropriate treatment and harassment at the workplace, which endangers my health.

The events started on [Date] and have manifested as follows:
- [Event 1]
- [Event 2]

According to the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the employer must take action to eliminate harassment upon becoming aware of it. I request you to investigate the matter immediately and inform me of the measures you intend to take.

[My Name]

I request a written response by [Date] on how the matter is progressing. If the matter does not progress, I will have to contact the Occupational Safety and Health Authority (AVI).

[My Name]

hero.title: Survival Guide
hero.subtitle: When you are in the eye of the storm, we find shelter for you. Here you will find action plans, calming techniques, and the right helpers.

phase1.label: Phase 1: Acute Situation
phase1.title: Secure Yourself
phase1.description: If you have just experienced something bad, the most important thing is to restore a sense of safety. Do not make big decisions (like resigning) while in panic.

step1.content: Go to the bathroom, take a walk, or go home (report sick). You have no obligation to listen to shouting or insults.

step2.content: Log only: who, what, where, when. Do not analyze yet. Just save the facts.

step3.content: Call a partner, friend, or occupational health. Do not remain alone with the experience.

phase2.label: Phase 2: Stabilization
phase2.title: Build Defense
phase2.description: When the acute shock subsides, it is time to start collecting evidence and protecting your position.

step1.content: Use the log tool in this app. Log retrospectively all events you remember.

step2.content: Read your employment contract, occupational health guidelines, and equality plan. Knowledge is power.

step3.content: Get a document about your symptoms (insomnia, anxiety). It is important evidence that work affects health.

phase3.label: Phase 3: Resolution
phase3.title: Act or Exit
phase3.description: When you are stronger and have evidence, you can choose to fight or make a strategic exit.

step1.content: Use the ready-made templates in the reporting tool (e.g. occupational safety notification).

step2.content: If you want to leave, negotiate an exit package with the support of a union lawyer. Do not just leave empty-handed.

breathing.title: 5-5-5 Breathing
breathing.description: A physiological way to lower heart rate and stop panic reaction.

questions.text: According to international studies, what is the prevalence of workplace bullying?
questions.explanation: International studies consistently show that 10-15% of employees experience systematic bullying.

questions.text: How many employees globally have experienced some form of violence or harassment at work during their career (ILO 2023)?
questions.explanation: ILO's first global study in 2023 showed that 23% of employed adults, or about 750 million employees globally, have experienced violence or harassment.

questions.text: Who is the most likely workplace bully?
questions.explanation: Studies show that a manager or supervisor is the most typical bully. Power hierarchy and misuse of positional power are key factors.

questions.text: What is the duration criterion for systematic bullying (Einarsen et al.)?

options.label: Once a week for at least a month
Repeatedly (e.g. weekly) and regularly for at least 6 months

questions.explanation: Einarsen defines bullying as acts that occur repeatedly and regularly (e.g. weekly) over a long period (usually at least 6 months).

questions.text: What proportion of employees have likely witnessed workplace bullying?
questions.explanation: Over 80% of employees have likely witnessed bullying at some point. This makes bystanders a much larger group than actual victims.

questions.text: What term refers to a supervisor questioning an employee's memory, perception, and sanity?
questions.explanation: Gaslighting is psychological violence where the victim is made to doubt their own reality. It silences the victim effectively.

questions.text: What is the purpose of 'constructive discharge'?
questions.explanation: The goal is to make the employee resign voluntarily, avoiding dismissal procedures. Making tasks meaningless is a common tactic.

questions.text: What does DARVO stand for?

options.label: Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim and Offender

questions.explanation: DARVO is a manipulation tactic: Deny the abuse, Attack the victim's credibility, and Reverse roles so the offender plays the victim.

questions.text: Which is a typical form of 'withholding information'?

options.label: Employee is denied access to critical info

questions.explanation: Information is power. Withholding it sets the subordinate up for failure.

questions.text: What are 'Flying Monkeys' in workplace bullying?
questions.explanation: Bullying is rarely a dyad. The bully gathers supporters who participate or silently approve.

questions.text: Which personality trio (Dark Triad) predicts bullying behavior best?
questions.explanation: The Dark Triad consists of Machiavellianism, Narcissism, and Psychopathy, predicting manipulative and unempathetic behavior.

questions.text: According to studies, which Dark Triad trait is the strongest predictor of bullying?
questions.explanation: Machiavellianism is the strongest single predictor, explaining a significant part of the variation.

questions.text: What does the Dark Tetrad add to the Triad?
questions.explanation: The Dark Tetrad adds Sadism (everyday sadism), deriving pleasure from others' suffering.

questions.text: Why is bullying often ignored in organizations?
questions.explanation: Organizations often protect 'star performers' who bring results, even if their leadership style destroys people.

questions.text: What percentage of victims lose their job due to bullying (WBI)?
questions.explanation: WBI studies show that a majority (67-77%) of victims lose their job, either quitting or being fired.

questions.text: What is the 'Bystander Effect'?

options.label: People intervene more when others are present
People don't intervene, expecting others to do so

questions.explanation: Responsibility 'diffuses' when multiple people are present, making intervention less likely.

questions.text: Which bystander role relates to best work engagement?
questions.explanation: Active defending predicts best work engagement for the bystander themselves.

questions.text: What proportion of witnesses do not report what they saw?
questions.explanation: About 55% of witnesses do not report, which is alarmingly high.

questions.text: What is the most common reason for not reporting?
questions.explanation: Cynicism and belief that the organization won't do anything is the top reason (55%).

questions.text: How does the number of passive bystanders affect the victim?
questions.explanation: More passive bystanders amplify the negative effect on the victim.

questions.text: What physical symptoms does long-term bullying cause?
questions.explanation: Bullying triggers severe physiological stress reactions.

questions.text: What is the cardiovascular risk ratio for victims compared to non-victims?
questions.explanation: Risk is 2.3 times higher. Long-term stress is toxic to the body.

questions.text: How does witness well-being compare to victims?
questions.explanation: Witnesses are also traumatized. Watching injustice is psychologically heavy.

questions.text: Where does bullying bank as a stressor?
questions.explanation: It is the 2nd most common stressor after excessive workload.

questions.text: How many victims have told someone?
questions.explanation: Only about half tell anyone. Shame and fear prevent speaking out.

questions.text: Who is responsible for intervening in bullying?
questions.explanation: The employer has a legal duty to intervene immediately when aware.

questions.text: What is the effect of teaching DARVO?
questions.explanation: Knowledge is armor. Recognizing the pattern weakens its effect.

questions.text: Which industry suffers most from bullying?
questions.explanation: Health and social care top the statistics due to hierarchy and pressure.

questions.text: Which gender is more likely to be a victim?
questions.explanation: Women are more often victims (57%), while men are overrepresented as bullies.

questions.text: How many female bullies choose a female victim?
questions.explanation: Female bullies target other women 71% of the time.

questions.text: What is the strongest protective factor?
questions.explanation: Culture eats strategy for breakfast. If management doesn't support zero tolerance, policies are useless.

questions.text: Which is an ineffective prevention method?
questions.explanation: Declarations are not enough if structures don't support them.

questions.text: What does 'culture of silence' mean?
questions.explanation: It allows abuse to continue because no one dares to speak.

questions.text: What is 'institutional betrayal'?
questions.explanation: When the organization that should protect you turns its back, it causes deep trauma.

questions.text: How many UK healthcare workers experienced bullying?
questions.explanation: Public sector pressures are a global challenge.
